subject.title: Orphaned lock files not cleared on gateway restart when PID matches current process

question: Should #49603 remain the focused current-PID session-lock lifecycle tracker, or should maintainers fold the remaining work into a broader session-lock recovery issue after defining the safe reclaim policy?
rationale: The code can identify some self-owned orphan locks today, but reclaiming locks from a live current PID crosses a data-integrity boundary that automation should not decide from source inspection alone.

options.title: Keep Focused Tracker
options.body: Keep #49603 open as the focused same-PID session-lock tracker and have maintainers define the reclaim semantics before another fix PR is queued.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Recovery Work
options.body: Move the remaining runtime/recovery cases under a broader open session-lock orchestration issue and close this only after linking the canonical owner.

options.title: Close Only Boot-Sweep Scope
options.body: Close this issue only if maintainers explicitly decide the original boot-cleanup ask is complete and create or link a narrower issue for runtime current-PID lock leaks.

recommendation.title: Keep Focused Tracker
recommendation.body: Keep #49603 open as the focused same-PID session-lock tracker and have maintainers define the reclaim semantics before another fix PR is queued.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter authored the current-main post-abort lock fix and appears in the recent session-lock history most directly connected to the remaining policy boundary.
